node_sequence.text: Any sign of head or neck injury?

Check AIRWAY, BREATHING, CIRCULATION (ABCs). Start timing the duration of the convulsions. Place an intravenous (i.v.) line if possible. Ensure the person is in a safe place. Do not leave the person alone. Do not put anything in the mouth. For a person with possible head injury, neuroinfection, or focal deficits, refer urgently to hospital.
SPECIAL POPULATION: Is the woman in the second half of pregnancy OR up to 1 week post partum AND has no past history of epilepsy?

Give medication to stop convulsions. If no i.v. established: give diazepam rectally or midazolam buccally/intranasally. If i.v. established: start normal saline, glucose, and give emergency medication (diazepam or lorazepam i.v.).
Have the convulsions stopped within 10 minutes of 1st dose of emergency medication?
Has the person had convulsive movements lasting longer than 1-2 minutes?
Convulsive seizures unlikely. Consult a specialist for recurrent episodes.
